correctness.rationale: The product construction is coordinatewise and Proposition 3.2 converts coordinatewise induced shadowing to the source definition of shadowing map. L-shadowing is preserved because finitely many coordinate errors tending to zero have max tending to zero. Reflection to a factor uses an embedding that inserts exact orbits in all passive coordinates; projection then preserves the pseudo-orbit-map axiom and the required shadowing/limit-shadowing estimates. For self-tuning, Proposition 5.3 reduces the property to a local sequence-discrepancy estimate; under the active-factor embedding the product discrepancy equals the factor discrepancy exactly, while in the product direction every factor discrepancy is bounded by the product discrepancy.

value.rationale: The 2025 source makes existence of a continuous pseudo-orbit selector strictly stronger than ordinary shadowing and builds a hierarchy of selector regularity. The finite-product theorem gives an exact structural test at three successive levels: product formation neither creates nor destroys selector existence, L-selector regularity, or self-tuning. This supplies a reusable reduction from finite product systems to factors and sharply distinguishes these levels from the stronger invariance levels, where the factor argument does not automatically preserve the defining commutation identities.
